title: Onboarding probe anchoring & rollout scenario library
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
This document is a practical library of probe anchoring patterns and rollout scenarios to use during model onboarding and promotion. It focuses on how to attach (anchor) probes to service-level slices, how to interpret multi-signal telemetry during staged rollouts, and prescriptive rollback/mitigation playbooks. The goal is to standardize onboarding behaviors for mixed-latency, quantized, and cache-sensitive models so decisions across teams are repeatable and auditable.

Scope
- Applies to model onboarding for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Covers probes used by the eval harness, shadow load, and canary traffic.
- Includes guidance for quantization-aware probes and KV-cache warmup probes.
- Does not replace service-specific SLO documents; it complements them by specifying probe-to-SLO anchoring.

Why anchoring matters
Anchoring ties probe results to an explicit acceptance decision. Without anchoring, teams frequently mismatch probe signals (e.g., token-level coherence vs. p95 latency). Anchoring rules ensure we enforce the correct contract for: correctness (quality), latency, token-cost, and stability under quantization and caching.

Key concepts (short definitions)
- Anchor: a binding between a probe (input set + measurement) and a target service slice or SLO.
- Probe family: a curated set of probes meant to exercise a single class of failure (e.g., long-context coherence probes).
- Anchor contract: the telemetry signals, thresholds and aggregation method used to accept/rollback.
- Warmup probe: a probe designed to populate KV cache and prime model kernels for stable performance.

Scenario catalog (selection)
1) Latency-sensitive canary (API-to-user-facing route)
- Anchor: route=predictive-text, SLO=p95_latency<=300ms
- Probe family: short prompt micro-bursts, payloads sized to real traffic (avg token <= 20)
- Signals: p95 latency, p99 latency, error rate, streaming-backpressure events
- Acceptance criteria (example): p95 <= 300ms AND error_rate < 0.5% over 10k requests; if p99 > 600ms trigger mitigation.

2) Coherence-first shadow rollout (background evaluators)
- Anchor: service_slice=document-summarization, SLO=semantic-fidelity-delta<=0.03 (vs baseline)
- Probe family: long-context summary probes, semantic-similarity scoring (embedding cosine + human anchoring), stochastic seeds (n=5)
- Signals: fidelity_delta (mean), coherence-stability-index (95% CI), annotator disagreement rate
- Acceptance criteria: fidelity_delta <= 0.03 AND annotator_disagreement <= 12% over sample of 2k probes.

3) Quantization-focused rollout (mixed precision)
- Anchor: quant_profile=q8_2, SLO=per-token-coherence-resilience>=0.98
- Probe family: adversarial priming + perturbation noise sweep
- Signals: coherence-regression-rate, token-level entropy shift, memory-alloc-failures on 2 GPU types
- Acceptance criteria: coherence-regression-rate < 2% and no memory alloc failures in 1k-run smoke test.

4) KV-cache warmup + cold-start guard
- Anchor: tenant_tier=dedicated, SLO=cold-start-p95 <= 500ms after 30s idle
- Probe family: burst of representative multi-turn sessions to populate KV cache (session length distribution modeled after production)
- Signals: cold-start_p95, incremental latency per call, cache-hit-rate, trailing-token-overhead
- Acceptance criteria: cache_hit_rate >= 85% after warmup load AND cold-start_p95 <= 500ms.

Decision matrix (signals -> action)
Use the table below during canaries. Aggregate signals over the canary window. This is a compact decision grid — treat as legally binding for promotions when using the standard onboarding pipeline.
| Signal (window) | Green | Yellow | Red | Action |
|-----------------|-------|--------|-----|--------|
| p95 latency (30m) | <=300ms | 300-450ms | >450ms | Continue / Hold / Rollback to previous model |
| fidelity_delta (2k probes) | <=0.03 | 0.03-0.06 | >0.06 | Promote / Investigate / Rollback |
| error rate (30m) | <=0.5% | 0.5-1.5% | >1.5% | Continue / Hold & throttling / Rollback & throttle traffic |
| coherence-regression-rate (sample) | <2% | 2-5% | >5% | Promote-small / Annotation repair required / Rollback + freeze rollout |

Anchoring pattern templates
- SLO-anchor template (short):
  - anchor_id: <service>-<slice>-<probe_family>
  - primary_metrics: [metric1, metric2, ...]
  - aggregation: rolling_mean/median/p95 over <window>
  - decision_thresholds: {green: X, yellow: Y, red: Z}
  - telemetry_sources: [prod-metrics, eval-harness, shadow-trace]

- Probe-job spec (example YAML snippet):
  ```yaml
  probe_job:
    name: kv-warmup-primer-v1
    anchor: inference-service/document-summarization-kv-warmup
    schedule: one-off
    parallelism: 40
    sample_bucket: prod-replay/tenant-priority-1
    run_timeout: 120s
    metrics_emit: [latency_ms,p99_latency,cache_hits,error_rate]
    artifact_retention: 90d
  ```

Telemetry & signal handling (best practices)
- Prefer relative deltas over absolute thresholds for quality metrics ("fidelity_delta vs baseline"), except for latency where absolute thresholds better reflect UX.
- Always declare primary and fallback telemetry sources. Example: primary=prod-metrics, fallback=shadow-mesh, tertiary=eval-harness samples.
- Use bootstrap sampling (n>=5 seeds) for non-deterministic probes and report mean+CI.
- Annotator priming: for any semantic scoring probe, include a mandatory human-anchoring step for the first 500 failing probes.

Rollout playbook (step-by-step)
1) Preflight (offline checks)
   - Run the quant and unit-fidelity checks locally (min 1k synthetic seeds).
   - Verify model artifact signature and quant-profile metadata (quant_profile field present).
   - Create anchor contract and publish it to the onboarding tracker.
2) Shadow stage (no user traffic)
   - Launch 24h shadow run against 1% of production traffic split to avoid tenant skew.
   - Run warmup probes within first 10 minutes to populate caches.
   - Evaluate telemetry against anchor contract: if any Red-level signal fires, stop shadow and open a regression ticket.
3) Micro-canary (internal traffic)
   - Serve 0.5% traffic routed from internal test accounts.
   - Run full probe family at 5x rate to accelerate signal collection.
   - Hold for at least 2 business hours or until 10k probe samples are collected.
4) Gradual ramp (progressive percentages)
   - Ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%, waiting 30-60 minutes at each step.
   - At each step, evaluate anchor contract and run warmup probes if cache-sensitive.
5) Post-promote monitoring
   - For 72 hours after 100% promote, run nightly targeted probes focused on high-risk slices (long context, high-cost tenants).

Rollback & mitigation cookbook (quick actions)
- If Red fidelity_delta: immediate rollback to previous pinned model, issue a regression alert with probe artifacts and top-50 failing inputs.
- If latency regression but quality OK: throttle non-critical routes, enable burst-only routing to dedicated capacity, and roll forward a kernel-optimized variant if available.
- If cache instability (cache_hit_rate drop >15%): temporarily increase cache warmup rate and allocate short-lived dedicated warmup pods.
- If quant-induced memory allocation errors: revert to a lower quant profile for the affected fleet and schedule quant re-tuning.

Playbook for regression triage (when anchor fires Yellow/Red)
1) Gather artifacts: probe inputs, model version, quant_profile, kernel selection logs, and a trace for the slowest 5 requests.
2) Run local micro-replay with identical seed(s) and environment to reproduce.
3) Run bisect on model versions / quant variants if shadow cohort exists.
4) If root cause is prompt-sensitive, tag probes as "prompt-failure" and escalate to prompt engineering with top-20 failing prompts.
5) If root cause is infra (GPU OOM, slow kernel), assign to runtime team, provide kernel profile and top traces.

Ownership, tagging, and auditability
- Every anchor contract must include: owner (pager/team), primary contact email, and a rollout changelog.
- Tag probe jobs with: anchor_id, model_version, quant_profile, and commit_sha.
- Retain probe artifacts for 90 days by default and 365 days for enterprise-sensitive tenants.

FAQ
Q: How many probes are enough in a canary?
A: Target at least 10k probe executions for latency-sensitive routes and 2k probe executions for semantic/coherence probes. For low-volume tenants, synthesize extra probes using the probe fabricator.

Q: Can we promote if one metric is Yellow but others are Green?
A: Yes, with explicit mitigations and a documented hold period. The anchor contract must include allowed Yellow actions (example: limited-rate promote + 24h close monitoring).

Appendix A — Troubleshooting examples
- Example: p99 spikes during micro-canary caused by kernel fallback. Action: collect kernel selection logs, pin older kernel, and rerun micro-canary.
- Example: quant_residual coherence drift: run quant-shadow with wider temperature and multiple seeds, then re-run targeted annotator jobs.

Appendix B — Useful CLI snippets
- Trigger a one-off warmup probe job:
  $ ri probe run --job kv-warmup-primer-v1 --anchor inference-service/document-summarization-kv-warmup --parallel 40 --timeout 120s
- Fetch last 24h anchor telemetry:
  $ ri metrics query --anchor inference-service/document-summarization-kv-warmup --window 24h --agg p95,mean,error_rate

Related reading
- See "Onboarding fidelity SLA and noise budget manifest" for negotiation of fidelity_delta budgets.
- Refer to the quantization manifest for allowed quant profiles and rollback thresholds.
